cita: Chrysochos (2026). Mind-Tool: Domain Memory Architecture for AI Agents.
notes: Single-author production case study (90-day home-lab+VPS infra deployment), not a controlled experiment vs an academic benchmark. Memory Folder = versioned markdown files in Git (infra state, operational history/incidents, decision records, procedural runbooks) -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS, mem_tipos spans episodic(incidents)/semantic(infra state,decisions)/procedural(runbooks). Fig.3 caption explicitly names 'consolidation' of accumulated knowledge -> CONSOLIDACION. Table1: 147 files/8437 lines, 68% tasks automated, 2.3min(automated) vs 8.7min(human-assisted), 62% time reduction (15h/week), 94% success, 6% error(non-reasoning/network), 91% escalation accuracy, 34 reused workflows (5.8 avg reuse), 18 troubleshooting patterns. Fig.4: 85% time reduction vs manual, 73% vs stateless AI. No controlled ablation isolating memory presence (comparison to 'stateless AI'/manual baselines is informal/anecdotal, not measured on the same tasks) -> evidencia_tipo=MEDICION-COSTO;CUALITATIVA not ABLATION/BENCHMARK-E2E. Desired-State component = persisted conversational goal-tracking -> plan_estado=SI. Git version-control provides change-tracking but no explicit content verification/staleness-resolution mechanism -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO. Single-agent pattern (explicit contrast to Anthropic's two-agent pattern) -> multiagente=NO. F differs from F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL only): added WRITE, DOCS-VERSIONADO (git-versioned md files central to the architecture), COSTO (62%/94% quantified efficiency), CONSOLIDACION.

cita: Wu et al. (2026). LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues.
notes: Sec.3.3 formal Insert/Query context-gathering formulation is the core RQ3 measurement (mide_lectura=SI -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO required in F). 451 curated Qs over 5 abilities (static/dynamic/workflow/gotchas/premise) paired w/ 100-500-trajectory haystacks (25M/115M tokens). Two own baselines: AgentRunbook-R (S4.1, RAG: raw-state-slice pool + state-transition-event pool + procedure/hint-note pool, dense retrieval per pool -> VECTOR+EMBEDDINGS) and AgentRunbook-C (S4.2, stores trajectories as files, coding-agent harness searches/inspects at query time -> DOCS-ARCHIVOS+GREP-ARCHIVOS-like file exploration). Note pool explicitly 'consolidate[s] trajectory experience into compact reusable knowledge' -> CONSOLIDACION. Main results (S5, abstract): simple RAG state-slice 40.1%; AgentRunbook-R 57.8%; off-the-shelf Codex 69.3% at ~182s/query (6.9x slower than AgentRunbook-R); AgentRunbook-C best at 72.5% accuracy, 32% faster than Codex -> LATENCIA explicitly reported alongside accuracy (accuracy-latency Pareto frontier). Pilot studies (Fig.4): frontier LLMs w/o trajectory history top out at 14.1% (parametric knowledge insufficient); oracle-trajectory/oracle-slices+notes ablation isolates retrieval-vs-grounding difficulty -> ABLATION. F_screening confirmed (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO;PROCEDIMENTAL) + added WRITE(Insert API), CONSOLIDACION, COSTO(latency/query-cost central finding).

fallos_mitigaciones: Uncontrolled synthetic practice yields redundant/infeasible/uninformative tasks and can contaminate memory with misleading guidance from unfiltered trajectories; mitigated via Validator feasibility-gated admission (score=5/5 required before solver-memory insertion, Sec.3.4) plus proposer-memory practice-history tracking of over/under-used tools to avoid redundancy (Sec.3.3). Table2 component ablation: removing the Validator raises Infeasible-Task% and lowers Unique-Tools/Weighted-Recall (e.g. AppWorld all-disabled=Naive Task Generation drops to 47.8/26.8 TGC/SGC vs full PREPING 83.7/70.2).
cita: Choi et al. (2026). PREPING: Building Agent Memory without Tasks.
notes: Pre-task (cold-start) procedural memory construction w/o any target-environment task data: Proposer/Solver/Validator loop (Sec.3.2) builds proposer memory Mprop (construction-time control state: practice history + grounded-environment view) and solver memory Msol (deployment-facing playbook, distilled into 'compact procedural bullets' -> CONSOLIDACION per reflector-curator style of ACE). Validator gates admission (feasibility score must be 5) -> ADMISION + FIDELIDAD (grounding/feasibility verification before write). Table1 main results: PREPING improves over no-memory Base by +17.1pp AppWorld, +19.3pp BFCL v3, +5.4pp MCP-Universe avg; exceeds ACE-Offline on AppWorld, competitive w/ ACE-Online. Deployment cost 2.99x lower (AppWorld) / 2.23x lower (BFCL v3) than ACE-Online when frozen (no online memory-update calls) -> COSTO. Table2 ablates Validator/Env.Info/Practice-History components on AppWorld+BFCL v3. Table3/Fig.3: PREPING+ACE warm-start improves AppWorld 71.3->76.3 and mitigates online cold-start. Retrieval mechanism at deployment not specified (solver memory supplied wholesale to agent, no ranking/embedding/graph retrieval described) -> retrieval=NA. Solver/proposer memory scoped per target environment (not per-task, not cross-org) -> alcance=PROYECTO.

benchmarks: EvoMemBench (own; built from MemoryAgentBench, BFCL-Multiturn-LongContext/Base, CL-Bench, xbench-DeepSearch, WebWalkerQA, ALFWorld) vs LoCoMo/LongMemEval/StuLife/MemoryBench/Evo-Memory/MemoryArena
fallos_mitigaciones: Finding3: appended memory becomes net-negative at large context budgets (128K, several methods fall below no-memory baseline) because it 'can introduce noise or consume useful context space without adding sufficient information'; Finding4: aggressive short-term compression loses fine-grained execution details (MemAgent/MemoBrain underperform the no-memory baseline at 16K/32K/128K on I N E P-E XEC) -> implied mitigation is matching memory granularity/compression aggressiveness to task needs rather than uniform compression.
cita: Wang et al. (2026). EvoMemBench: Benchmarking Agent Memory from a Self-Evolving Perspective.
notes: Pure benchmark (mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA per rule5): compares 15 existing memory methods (retrieval-augmented BM25/Qwen3-Emb/GraphRAG, short-term MemAgent/MemoBrain, general long-term Mem0/A-MEM/MemOS/MemoryOS, procedural AWM/SkillWeaver/AgentKB/ACE/ReasoningBank, meta-evolution MemEvolve) + long-context baselines across 4 settings (in/cross-episode x knowledge/execution). mide_lectura=SI: whole benchmark measures downstream task success attributable to memory retrieval across settings (Sec.5, Table3-6) -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Sec.3.3 explicitly defines 'Execution evolution' memory content as 'task progress, intermediate results, tool outputs, unresolved subgoals, previous decisions' -> plan_estado=SI (RQ Q4 axis is literally what this axis measures). Finding2 (Table3): memory methods stronger at retention than 'revision' (updating/suppressing/replacing memory when later evidence conflicts with earlier evidence, FactConsolidation subset) = explicit staleness/consistency evaluation -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI, FIDELIDAD. Finding3/Finding5 = explicit NEGATIVO findings (memory underperforms no-memory baseline at large context / on easy cross-episode tasks). Token usage reported as efficiency metric (Fig.2) alongside accuracy -> COSTO-TOKENS/COSTO. Scope spans TAREA (in-episode) to PROYECTO (cross-episode, shared-context reuse across episodes, e.g. C ROSS E P-K NOW/T OOL groupings).

fallos_mitigaciones: Identifies 4 gaps in prior AutoSkill lines (Sec.1): creation-usage mismatch, no structured per-skill memory, static unvalidated skills, poor long-horizon context handling. Mitigated respectively via: built-in skill_create invoked from the runtime loop; per-skill .memory.md accumulating notes/failure-modes/quirks across tasks; unit-test-driven Evaluator that blocks registration until tests pass and auto-triggers Refiner on failure; adaptive short-term-memory compression + cross-session persistence. Table11 diagnostic ablation: memory-system-off round2 accuracy 60.0% vs memory-system-on 74.0% (+14.0pp), at comparable/lower token+latency cost (423.9k tok/295.4s on vs 408.4k tok/338.6s off).
cita: Lin et al. (2026). MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation.
notes: Multi-level memory: short-term (task context, adaptively compressed -> TRABAJO), long-term (persistent cross-session lessons/quirks -> SEMANTICA), and skill-level .memory.md per SKILL.md (per-skill accumulated experience -> PROCEDIMENTAL). Skill catalog metadata injected into system prompt, agent 'selects the most relevant skill during planning' -> retrieval=RANKING (no embeddings/graph described). Sec.3.2 Skill Management: refinement (update_skill on test-fail=ACTUALIZACION), merging of overlapping skills=CONSOLIDACION, pruning of unused/failing skills=OLVIDO; registration blocked until tests pass=ADMISION+FIDELIDAD. Headline SkillsBench: MUSE best human-skill accuracy 59.67% (+12.72pp vs no-skill), best self-created-skill 53.42% (all-task) beating Codex 47.52%/Claude Code 44.27%; self-created skills transfer to Hermes at 51.90% > Hermes-w/-human-skills 48.02% -> explicit cross-agent transfer experiment (Table1, unique among compared methods) -> multiagente=SI. Table11 (App.) isolated memory-system on/off ablation on SkillLearnBench: 74.0% vs 60.0% round-2 accuracy (+14.0pp) with token/turn/latency reported -> COSTO. F_screening (PROCEDIMENTAL;WRITE) confirmed + added CONSOLIDACION, FIDELIDAD, MULTIAGENTE, COSTO.

fallos_mitigaciones: Fixed memory-construction-retrieval (MCR) pipelines struggle with heterogeneous task-specific failure modes and drift out of alignment as the memory bank evolves in scale/structure, causing incomplete retrieval, noisy evidence, or ineffective use of retrieved memories (Sec.1). Mitigated by treating the whole MCR pipeline (not just the memory bank or prompts) as an evolvable program: an Evolving Agent diagnoses recurring failure modes from a version-tree of evaluation logs and applies failure-mode-guided edit-debug refinement (Sec.4).
cita: Liu et al. (2026). MemPro: Agentic Memory Systems as Evolvable Programs.
notes: MCR pipeline formalized Sec.3: memory-bank construction Mt=UPDATE(Mt-1,dMt) from segmented raw data (WRITE;ACTUALIZACION, EVENTO-DETERMINISTA per timestep) + iterative Research-Agent retrieval-integration-reflection loop over the bank. App.A.6 retrieval-tool ablation: 'module uses three retrieval channels: BM25 keyword retrieval, BAAI/bge-m3 semantic retrieval[EMBEDDINGS], and structural[page_index] retrieval'; BM25 most important channel (removing it drops accuracy 84.93->lower) -> RANKING+EMBEDDINGS, mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Fig.3 4-way component ablation on LoCoMo (w/o Code / w/o Version-Tree / w/o Iterative-Expansion / w/o Evolution) all show clear drops vs full MemPro (84.93 GPT-4o-mini / 81.23 Qwen3). Table1/Table2 SOTA across LongMemEval/LoCoMo (LLM-as-judge) and HotpotQA/NarrativeQA (F1); MemPro-5/10/15 = 5/10/15 evolution iterations, keeps improving (+1.59/+1.95 LongMemEval, +1.06/+1.20 LoCoMo across iteration bands). Fig.4 token-cost-vs-accuracy efficiency analysis (App.A: 'Token cost is computed over task-time inference only and excludes offline evolution calls') -> COSTO-TOKENS. No multi-agent memory sharing (single Memory Agent + single Research Agent) -> multiagente=NO; no staleness/provenance verification discussed -> fidelidad_procedencia=NO.
